extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of gasoline distribution facilities, control device manufacturers, state/federal regulators, and compliance officers (regulated industry and permitting authorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and implementation of EPA NSPS/NESHAP requirements for gasoline loading racks, VRUs, flares, and thermal oxidizers, including monitoring, performance testing, operating limits, recordkeeping, and applicability thresholds. Focused on demonstrating continuous compliance with TOC/TOC-as-propane emission limits and related parametric limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: VRU CEMS performance evaluation duration and 3-hour averaging rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of VRUs must conduct performance evaluations of their TOC continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS). The performance evaluation consists of a minimum of nine test runs, with each test run being a sampling traverse of a minimum of 21 minutes in duration. Thus, the performance evaluation is a minimum of 189 minutes in duration, which is approximately 3 hours. We selected a 3-hour average to be consistent with the duration of the performance evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nine runs × 21 minutes to justify a 3-hour average for VRU CEMS performance evaluation; align averaging period for operating limits with evaluation duration to ensure consistency between test and continuous monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of '3-hour rolling average' for monitored parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: 3-hour rolling average means the arithmetic mean of the previous thirty-six 5-minute periods of valid operating data collected, as specified, for the monitored parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid data excludes data collected during periods when the monitoring system is out of control, while conducting repairs associated with periods when the monitoring system is out of control, or while conducting required monitoring system quality assurance or quality control activities. The thirty-six 5-minute periods should be consecutive, but not necessarily continuous if operations or the collection of valid data were intermittent. (Finalized definition placed at 40 CFR 60.501a.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods to include/exclude from the 3-hour rolling average by control device type
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify time periods applicable to different control devices rather than using the general phrase 'all emissions from the loading event have cleared the control device.' For thermal oxidation systems, the operating limits apply at all times when liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks. If the immediately previous load of a cargo tank is not known, then the cargo tank must be assumed to be a gasoline cargo tank. Periods when there is no liquid product loading must be excluded from the 3-hour rolling average. For vapor recovery systems, the operating limits apply at all times that the vapor system is operating, because emissions can come from the regeneration of a carbon bed even though there is no liquid product loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add recordkeeping and reporting requirements related to periods when gasoline cargo tanks are being loaded and indicate whether cargo tanks are assumed to be gasoline cargo tanks because the previous load is unknown. Exclude non-loading periods from 3-hour averages for thermal oxidizers; include regeneration and other VRU operation periods for VRUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate VRU to minimize air or nitrogen intrusion with specified exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must 'operate the vapor recovery system to minimize air or nitrogen intrusion except as needed for the system to operate as designed for the purpose of removing VOC from the adsorption media or to break vacuum in the system and bring the system back to atmospheric pressure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with §60.12, the use of gaseous diluents to achieve compliance with a concentration-based standard is prohibited. The final provisions were revised to allow some purge air or nitrogen to be introduced while the unit is under vacuum and being regenerated as needed to effectively remove VOC from the adsorption media, but otherwise minimize intrusion to prevent dilution of emissions measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) determination and corresponding TOC emission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For the NSPS review the EPA determined that the BSER was VRU with submerged loading. For new bulk gasoline terminals the TOC emission limitation reflecting BSER is 1.0 mg/L (for systems with a VRU, a concentration of 550 ppmv TOC as propane). For modified or reconstructed bulk gasoline terminals the TOC limit reflecting BSER is 10 mg/L (for systems with a VRU, 5,500 ppmv TOC as propane).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits are finalized except that methane may be excluded from measured TOC (see separate reporting/test method requirements). The BSER determination drove the choice of control technology and numeric emission limits for new and modified facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of methane from measured TOC and related test/reporting changes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is allowing the exclusion of methane from the measured TOC for reasons discussed elsewhere in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With exclusion of methane, EPA finalizes additional test methods applicable for non-methane organic carbon and additional reporting requirements to indicate whether the measurement method used in the performance test or CEMS corrects for methane concentration. Corresponding recordkeeping and reporting provisions are finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate affected-facility definitions to limit modification applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize two separate affected facilities definitions for NSPS subpart XXa: 'gasoline loading rack affected facility' and 'collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing separate definitions expands equipment leak provisions to all equipment in gasoline service at the bulk gasoline terminal while ensuring equipment changes remote from loading racks and vapor processing systems do not trigger a modification to the loading rack affected facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow flare monitoring alternatives for thermal oxidation systems meeting 10 mg/L TOC
rubrics_metrics.description: Because flares can be used to comply with the 10 mg/L TOC emission limit and many thermal oxidation systems used in the gasoline distribution industry are enclosed combustors, the flare monitoring alternatives are appropriate for thermal oxidation systems required to meet the 10 mg/L emission limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify requirements for using one-time assessment of net heating value for vapors with consistent composition or a minimum net heating value as provided in 40 CFR 63.670(j)(6) when vapors from loading of different liquid products are processed by the flare or thermal oxidation system. Require facilities using this one-time assessment to monitor gasoline and total liquid product loading rates and maintain the ratio of gasoline to total liquid product loaded above levels in their application under 40 CFR 63.670(j)(6). For perimeter air-assisted flares or thermal oxidizers, gasoline loading rates must also be maintained at or above minimum gasoline loading rates specified in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time engineering assessment for flare tip velocity operating limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize provision at 40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3)(ix) for conducting a one-time engineering assessment as a means to demonstrate compliance with the flare tip velocity operating limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this compliance method is used, corresponding recordkeeping requirements for the one-time assessment are finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature operating limit for thermal oxidation systems (continuous compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For thermal oxidation systems EPA proposed and finalized continuous compliance with a temperature operating limit established as the lowest 3-hour average temperature from a compliant performance test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating limits apply at all times when liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks. Finalized because data showed exceedances of TOC limits occurred at temperatures below a threshold (e.g., <900°F for 35 mg/L), supporting temperature as a reasonable continuous compliance indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow pressure-monitoring alternative during performance tests or evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Add an alternative monitoring provision at 40 CFR 63.427(f) that allows pressure monitoring during performance tests or performance evaluations following the provisions in 40 CFR 60.503(d) to determine that the system is appropriately designed and operated at or below a pressure of 18 inches of water during product loading as an alternative to using a pressure CPMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities that have a pressure CPMS may use it for compliance, and additional language expressly provides pressure monitoring during performance tests or evaluations when intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area-source loading rack TOC limit and equivalents (NESHAP subpart BBBBBB)
rubrics_metrics.description: For area source large bulk gasoline terminals EPA finalized lowering allowable TOC emission limit from 80 mg/L to 35 mg/L. For loading racks controlled by VRUs EPA expresses this emission limit as a concentration limit of 19,200 ppmv TOC as propane on a 3-hour rolling average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For thermal oxidation systems, continuous compliance via temperature operating limit established as the lowest 3-hour average temperature from a compliant performance test; allow use of a 'flare monitoring alternative' as an alternative to the temperature operating limit for thermal oxidation systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balancing applicability and design thresholds (bulk gasoline plants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require vapor balancing between gasoline cargo tanks and gasoline storage vessels for bulk gasoline plants with a gasoline throughput over 4,000 gallons per day, assessed on an actual throughput basis using an annual averaging time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise threshold to be based on actual throughput (annual average) rather than maximum calculated design throughput. Add requirements to maintain records of gasoline throughput and the time frame in which to add vapor balancing controls if a plant newly triggers the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum pressure relief device opening pressure for fixed-roof storage tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize the appropriate minimum pressure relief device opening pressure for fixed roof storage tanks at 18 inches of water column (0.65 psia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected proposed 2.5 psig as not technically feasible for many atmospheric storage tanks and not cost-effective given tank replacement costs. Use existing industry expectation that relief devices open at pressures not less than 18 inches water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative monitoring protocols for thermal oxidation systems at area sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider allowing alternative monitoring protocols to temperature CPMS for area sources complying with a 35 mg/L TOC limit; alternatives include pilot flame monitoring and more substantive alternatives to prevent over-assisting of air-assisted combustors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded temperature is a reasonable indicator but proposed a more rigorous alternative that ensures the combustion unit is not over-assisted (e.g., require proper operation of air-assist blower and vapor line valve, multispeed blower operation tied to vapor flow rates, and vapor line valve settings to prevent very low flows). The alternative is designed to ensure good combustion during low-flow periods that may not be represented in performance tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net heating value (NHV) continuous monitoring or initial assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize requirements to either continuously monitor the net heating value of the vapors discharged to the flare or thermal oxidation system or to perform an initial assessment to determine a minimum gasoline loading rate operating limit that ensures high combustion efficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility cannot meet the NHV_dil operating limit based on the minimum gasoline loading rate operating limit, it can determine a minimum auxiliary fuel addition rate (or adjust air-assist rates) needed to ensure good combustion efficiencies at low flow rates. Facilities may use sampling of heat content and assessment of air addition rates to determine if auxiliary fuel is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for CEMS on VRU-controlled loading racks and limited-outage alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed to require CEMS for VRU-controlled loading racks to directly assess compliance with the TOC emission limit. However, EPA sought to provide an alternative to using a CEMS that could be used for limited periods of CEMS outages, but not as an ongoing indefinite alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outage alternative is based on regeneration cycles normalized by product loading quantities derived from recent CEMS operating data; this follows many requirements in existing NESHAP alternative protocols but bases operating parameters on data that demonstrated compliance when the CEMS was operating. Facilities should maintain records to justify regeneration-cycle-based operating parameters during CEMS outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reporting to support monitoring and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize recordkeeping and reporting requirements that correspond to revisions (e.g., excluding methane from TOC measurements, maintaining ratio of gasoline to total product loaded, minimum gasoline loading rates, one-time assessments, one-time engineering assessments, periods when cargo tanks are assumed to be gasoline cargo tanks, and CEMS outage alternative data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: report whether measurement method corrects for methane, monitor gasoline and total liquid product loading rates, maintain records of gasoline throughput and averaging time for applicability, record assumptions when previous cargo tank load is unknown, retain one-time assessment and engineering assessment documentation used to support alternative compliance methods.
